Feature: D-hold now skips boot ceremony straight into Sol in either flight mode, and orrery-mode arrival now does a proper camera zoom-in with orbit lines fading in as you clear the star's glow, instead of orbit lines popping/vanishing prematurely. Traces to the flight-reliability/orrery-coherence thread you flagged in UAT on 2026-07-19.

Where this stands: unit tests are fully green (1316/1316, plus the new AC3 pure-geometry suite at 29/29). But 4 of the 6 ACs (AC1 D-hold skip, AC2 mode-semantics preservation, AC4 zoom-in arrival, AC5 orbit fade threshold) are integration-layer, live-required checks that only got a static code read this pass — nobody has actually driven the running app yet. I'm handing those 4 to working-Claude (main thread) to drive live via chrome-devtools before this can be called integration-verified.

One thing worth knowing before you look at it yourself: reading the code turned up a specific, plausible bug in how AC4 (the zoom-in) and AC5 (the orbit fade) interact — the fade-factor calculation may be reading the camera's final resting distance instead of its current smoothed distance during the zoom, which would mean orbit lines show at full brightness from the very start of the arrival animation instead of fading in as you approach. That's exactly the kind of thing that would be obvious watching it but invisible in a code read or a headless test. Working-Claude should check this specifically when driving the live pass.

For your own UAT (AC6 — "does the whole entry sequence read as one coherent grammar"): hold off until working-Claude confirms the 4 integration checks above are actually green, especially the orbit fade-in. Once that's confirmed, the thing to look at yourself: boot the game fresh, hold D through the splash screen into both the ORRERY and HELM chooser buttons separately, and watch (a) no title/intro ceremony flashes at all, (b) the camera does a visible zoom-in on arrival rather than snapping straight to overview, (c) orbit lines are invisible at first and fade smoothly in as the camera glides closer, and (d) HELM-mode D-hold still lands you in a normal flying state with no stray auto-warp or self-flight. Whether all of that reads as "one coherent entry" rather than a pile of separate effects is your call to make, not mine.
